profile.summary: I build systems that help people solve hard problems at scale.Throughout my career, I've been driven by a simple belief: exceptional people, equipped with the right tools, communities, and opportunities, can accomplish extraordinary things. Whether through AI, education, infrastructure, or competitive programming, I enjoy building systems and organizations where talent can grow, collaborate, and compound over time.Today, I serve as Chief Architect at Probook, where I help build AI-native systems that transform how home service businesses operate. Previously, I worked at Google Research and Two Sigma, developing infrastructure and platforms that enabled large-scale research, machine learning, and decision-making.Beyond industry, I've spent more than a decade investing in technical talent development. I teach Computer Science at Columbia University, serve as Director of Internships at the ICPC Foundation, coach ICPC and IOI teams worldwide, and help organize international programming competitions, training camps, and educational initiatives. Working with aspiring engineers and problem solvers has been one of the most rewarding parts of my career.I'm particularly interested in AI-native systems, scalable infrastructure, education at scale, and the development of exceptional technical talent. I enjoy working at the intersection of research and production - turning ambitious ideas into systems that create lasting impact.If you're building ambitious products, advancing AI, strengthening technical communities, or investing in the next generation of builders and researchers, I'd be happy to connect.

volunteer_experiences.description:
I contributed to the growth and success of the ICPC Internship Program, which evolved from a 2023 pilot into a high-impact initiative with outstanding results: 339 applications received, 79 internships completed, and an average satisfaction rating of 9.6/10.

Program Overview:
Interns play a vital role in developing and maintaining key ICPC infrastructure, including the Problem Archive, North America regional websites, ICPC Journal - The Journal of Competitive Learning, mobile applications, and contest platforms. The program also provides F-1 OPT support, technical training, and career development resources.

Impact & Outcomes:
Alumni have gone on to work at leading companies such as Google, Amazon, Citadel, and Two Sigma. The Online Training platform has delivered 135 masterclasses, reaching over 1,500 members of the ICPC Discord community.

Technical Contributions:
Deliverables include complete website redesigns, standardized templates for regional contests, automated tools for contest directors, and comprehensive archival systems to preserve ICPC’s competitive programming legacy.

This program exemplifies how targeted internships can drive organizational innovation while launching successful technical careers, creating a scalable model for competitive programming education.

I serve as Chair of the Competitive Learning Institute (CLI) Symposium at the International Collegiate Programming Contest (ICPC) World Finals. The CLI Symposium is a vital part of the ICPC World Finals, offering a platform for thought leaders to share insights and foster meaningful discussions on competitive programming and related topics.

As a volunteer, I hold significant leadership and organizational responsibilities. I play a key role in curating the symposium's content, coordinating with speakers, and ensuring the smooth execution of the event. This involvement reflects my strong commitment to advancing education and collaboration within the competitive programming community.

projects.title: Stock Options Trading Platform
projects.description:
Made a financial platform mainly for stock options/volatility traders. Check out the IV Surface Graph page and the options page to see my options calculator. It calculates the price of the options given the change in the price of the underlying stock. I noticed that websites offering this feature use the Black-Scholes Model, which is not applicable to American options, so I used the Binomial Option Pricing Model.

As for the technical aspect, I used React and NextJS for the front-end and routing. I also made a Flask API to handle most of the calculations. The data for this website is scraped at 6:30 AM every weekday morning right before the markets open using my Python script image hosted as a AWS Batch Job. It uses the AWS Event Bridge to dump the data to a PostgreSQL database hosted as an AWS RDS instance at a specific time.

Overall, I learned a lot by building this project. Mainly, how to set up AWS cloud infrastructure and handle a lot of computation-heavy traffic using multithreading in Flask.

This website relies on a lot of data scraped from the internet, so it might feel a little slow. However, due to the expensive nature of financial data, I had to make do with free data.

profile.headline: Enterprise GTM at Probook
profile.title: Enterprise GTM
profile.summary:
My career in enterprise software has been built with intention — from inside sales to mid-market to enterprise, always moving toward the complexity and scale that I find most rewarding.

I started at BuildingConnected as the 35th employee. Over three years, a small team of us helped to build that company from $0 to $20M in ARR — learning how to sell before the brand could sell for us. I was consistently one of the top producers on the team during that run, and Autodesk ultimately acquired us for $275M. I came away with a deep appreciation for what a committed group of people can do when everyone is rowing in the same direction.

At Autodesk, I've spent 7+ years progressing from mid-market into enterprise, where I now work with some of the largest AECO firms in the world. I've carried $25M+ in cumulative quota, closed multi-year, multi-million dollar platform agreements, and earned Presidents Club twice. Those results reflect the SEs, CSMs, product partners, and cross-functional teams around me as much as anything I did on my own — enterprise selling is a team sport, and the best deals I've closed have been the ones where everyone brought their best.

I'm a certified MEDDIC practitioner, an informal mentor to the reps around me, and someone who genuinely believes that building great teams is how you build great revenue. My deepest experience is in AEC and construction technology, but the things I care most about — solving complex problems, earning trust, and making the people around me better — aren't limited to any one industry.
